newsitem.title: UK: GROBBELAAR ON SOCCER RETRIAL IN BRITAIN.
newsitem.headline: GROBBELAAR ON SOCCER RETRIAL IN BRITAIN.

text.p: Soccer stars Bruce
Grobbelaar, John Fashanu and Hans Segers stood trial on
Wednesday for the second time on charges of conspiring to fix
English premier league matches.
It was the most sensational British case of its kind for 30
years.
Zimbabwean-born Grobbelaar -- who won six league titles with
Liverpool -- fellow goalkeeper Segers and retired striker
Fashanu, as well as Malaysian businessman Heng Suan Lim, all
deny the charges.
They are accused of conspiring together to give and accept
gifts of money as inducements to influence the outcome of soccer
matches improperly or as rewards for having done so.
If convicted, they could face sentences of up to seven years
in jail and unlimited fines.
The defendants' first trial, which lasted eight weeks and
was estimated to have cost one million pounds ($1.6 million),
ended in anti-climax on March 4 when the jury failed to reach a
verdict on any of the charges.
Prosecutors decided two days later on a retrial.
The first day of the second trial was taken up by legal
argument and jury selection in front of Crown Court Judge
Charles McCullough in the southern town of Winchester.
Grobbelaar, wearing a dark jacket and carrying a briefcase,
looked grimly determined as he entered court. "I'll wait until
the end of the trial before I make a comment," he said.
The defendants as well as Fashanu's wife Melissa Kassa-Mapsi
were charged after an police inquiry into alleged match-fixing
and corruption. Charges against Kassa-Mapsi were later dropped.
The case, triggered by media allegations in November 1994
about the activities of an Asian betting syndicate in English
soccer, has generated worldwide interest.
Premier league games attract heavy betting in Britain and in
Asia on both the result and the precise score.
The trial is the first of its kind since three players from
Sheffield -- including two England internationals --
were imprisoned for four months in 1964 and banned from soccer
for life for fixing a match on which they had laid bets.
Grobbelaar, 39, moved to Southampton from Liverpool and now
plays for second division Plymouth. He is the most successful
goalkeeper in English club football after winning a clutch of
medals during his 13-year career with Liverpool.
Dutchman Segers, 35, played a few games last season for
non-league Woking while Fashanu, 33, who made his name with
Wimbledon, retired with a knee injury shortly after moving to
Aston Villa in 1994.
Grobbelaar denies a charge of accepting 40,000 pounds from
Fashanu to influence the result of a Newcastle United versus
Liverpool game in November 1993, when Grobbelaar was playing for
Liverpool. Newcastle won 3-0.
Fashanu, a television presenter and businessman who played
twice for England, denies giving Grobbelaar the money as a
reward for having improperly influenced or attempted to
influence the outcome of the match.
He also denies giving Segers 19,000 pounds as a reward after
Wimbledon's 3-0 defeat at Liverpool in October 1994. Segers
denied accepting any money.
Grobbelaar also denies a charge of accepting 2,000 pounds
from his former business partner, Chris Vincent, in November
1994 for throwing an unspecified match. Grobbelaar was
transferred to Southampton before the 1994-95 season.
($ = 0.611 British pounds)
